key_insight: Tuning the flame-spraying O2/C2H2 ratio strongly changes Ni–Cr–B–Si coating quality, with higher ratios generally producing denser, smoother, and better-adhered coatings.
engineering_relevance: This gives a practical process-control lever for optimizing self-fluxing spray coatings on corrosion-resistant steel in wear- and corrosion-critical applications.
method: Flame-sprayed Ni–Cr–B–Si self-fluxing coatings onto AISI 321 stainless steel using a Metal Coat 6PM-II system.
Varied the oxygen-to-acetylene ratio at 1.0, 1.1, and 1.2 to adjust thermal conditions.
Used Accuraspray 4.0 and post-test characterization to measure microstructure, porosity, microhardness, roughness, and adhesion.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports porosity dropping from 1.97 ± 0.13% to 0.90 ± 0.09%, roughness from 4.70 ± 0.09 μm to 2.99 ± 0.11 μm, and adhesion rising from 22.14 ± 4.3 MPa to 35.02 ± 3.9 MPa across the tested ratios, with peak microhardness of 1051.7 HV at O2/C2H2 = 1.1.
watch_item: The optimal ratio depends on which property is prioritized, since the highest microhardness occurred at 1.1 while the best density, smoothness, and adhesion were obtained at 1.2.
paper_title: EFFECT OF FLAME-SPRAYING TEMPERATURE ON THE PROPERTIES OF Ni–Cr–B–Si-BASED SELF-FLUXING COATINGS
